correctness.rationale: For H_{a,b}, each edge meets three different (unlabelled) parts, all parts having size 1 or 2. In a four-round EF game, preserving previously chosen vertices and the size and identity of each represented part is a partial isomorphism; at most four new parts of either size can be entered, so a,b may be truncated at four. There are exactly 19 allowed capped pairs because a+b>=3. Independently implemented complete rank-zero atomic diagrams (equality and ternary edge bits) and iterative all-vertex extension types T_{r+1}(tuple)={T_r(tuple,y):y vertex} partition those 19 cases into exactly twelve equivalence classes, with minimum representative vertex sizes 3,4,4,5,5,6,6,7,7,8,8,9. The complete Hintikka/EF recursion, unlike sampling, decides rank-four equivalence for those finite cases. The new independent enumeration agrees with source direct and orbit-compressed codes and confirms sharp nine-vertex representative bound inside this family. No expansion to arbitrary multipartite sizes or rank five is claimed.
